# Ryujinx shader translator (vendored subset)

Three projects from Ryujinx 1.3.2: `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common` and `Spv.Generator`, with these local changes:

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs`, `GenerateTextureSample`:
  - Texel offsets that are not constants (Maxwell AOFFI / TLD4.PTP offsets read from a register) are built with `OpCompositeConstruct` and passed as `Offset`. A four-offset gather becomes four one-offset gathers, each giving component w. Upstream wrote them as an `OpConstantComposite` with `ConstOffset(s)`, which is invalid SPIR-V; SPIRV-Cross threw `nullptr` and the shader never built (2026-10-18: 8 shaders in Wonder, Link's Awakening, Tears of the Kingdom and Age of Calamity). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.
  - Texture coordinates that are NaN are replaced by 0 (the `nfZero` select). This came with the first import.
- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Translation/Optimizations/BindlessElimination.cs`, `TryGetOperation` / `IsSameOperand`: a bindless handle that reaches the texture instruction through a phi is followed through the phis that feed it (a handle kept in a loop variable comes back through the loop's own phi), and two `constant buffer | constant` handles count as the same value. Upstream compared only the phi's direct inputs, so such handles fell to the texture-pool array of 32 (`*_t2d_cb0_40000000`), which cannot be bound; 218 pixel shaders in Monster Hunter Rise (2026-10-20). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/Instructions/InstEmitTexture.cs`, `EmitTex` (TLD 1D with integer coordinates only) and `EmitTexs` (TLDS `Texture1DLodZero`), with `IGpuAccessor.RecordTexelFetch1D`: Maxwell reads a 1D texture and a texture buffer with the same instruction, and the bound descriptor decides. When the texture type query does not answer "buffer", the read is translated as 2D at `(x & 0x3FFF, x >> 14)` instead of `(x, 0)`, and the handle is reported. A 1D texture (one row at most 16384 wide on the host) reads the same; the host binds a texture buffer in such a slot as a linear 2D texture of 16384-texel rows over its memory (`nvn_mtl.m` `tbuf_as_2d`). Upstream read `(x, 0)` and the host had only a dummy texture to give: the light and decal lists of Age of Calamity (at least 15,000 shaders) and Three Houses read zeros (2026-10-21). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/StructuredIr/AstOptimizer.cs`, `Optimize` / `UsedByCall`: a local that a call takes as an argument is not propagated. For SPIR-V, `StructuredProgram` copies every call argument into a local (SPIR-V passes them by pointer); propagating that local's expression into the call and removing the local left the call with a local no declaration made, and `CodeGen/Spirv` `GetLocalPointer` threw `KeyNotFoundException`: 1,894 of Viractal's 25,464 shaders, nearly all pixel shaders, did not translate (2026-10-25, the Android port). An operation with side effects (atomics, calls) is neither propagated nor removed: it stays in its assignment, so it runs once (Tears of the Kingdom lost unread atomic adds; Donkey Kong Bananza's read ones ran twice, 2026-11-03). Neither is a warp-wide operation (ballot, shuffle, vote, reduction, derivative): propagated into its one use it moved into the branch only one lane takes (Donkey Kong Bananza's REDUX reductions). Nor is a load of memory the shader writes (shared, local, storage, global): propagated into its use, it could move past the stores and barriers between them, which Ryujinx does not look for (the warp exchanges' reused words, 2026-11-04). Marked `nxnative:` in the code. Not yet in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin`, which is rebuilt on a Mac with `dmsh_chain.py --update-lock`; the Android port builds the translator from this source.

- `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/StructuredIr/StructuredProgram.cs`, `AddOperation` / `IsIntegerBuiltIn`: a load from memory, and of an integer built-in (thread, group and lane ids, the subgroup masks, vertex and instance indices), gets an integer variable instead of the table's float one: the words are bits (addresses, packed halves), and as floats a small integer is a denormal, which Vulkan lets a driver flush (2026-11-04, the Android port). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- Ampere (sm_86) frontend for NVN2 (Switch 2) shaders, `TranslationFlags.Ampere`: `Decoders/DecoderAmpere.cs`, `Decoders/AmpereOp.cs`, `Instructions/InstEmitAmpere*.cs`, with uniform, uniform predicate and shadow register files (`RegisterType`, `Translation/RegisterUsage.cs`, `Ssa.cs`). Maxwell code takes the old path, unchanged. Warp ops the Ampere code needs and Ryujinx's IR lacked: `Instruction.SubgroupReduce` (REDUX: a reduction over the subgroup, one a warp where the subgroup holds several, as the Adreno 750's compiler crashed on clustered ones) in `IntermediateRepresentation/Instruction.cs`, `StructuredIr/InstructionInfo.cs` and `CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs` (2026-11-03, Donkey Kong Bananza). `EmitterContext.PackHalf2x16` rounds to nearest even with denormals and infinities in integer operations, as NVIDIA converts, instead of the driver's packHalf2x16 (the Adreno 750's rounds toward zero and flushes denormals: Donkey Kong Bananza's upscaler network drew noise); LDSM and MOVM move halves as bits. Marked `nxnative:` where it touches upstream code.

- Warp exchanges in compute shaders go through workgroup memory: `Translation/WarpScratch.cs` (each lane stores its words at its linear invocation index in an array of their own, `warp_scratch`, then a subgroup barrier, the new IR instruction `SubgroupBarrier`; `ResourceManager.WarpScratchId` sizes it to the largest exchange. It has two buffers: Ampere blocks track which ones earlier exchanges' reads may still use, `EmitterContext.ScratchBusy`, through the blocks as the mirror below, and an exchange takes a free one with no barrier before its stores; other code takes buffer 0 after a barrier, and SHFL's helpers end with one), used by SHFL's helpers (`HelperFunctionManager`, `ShufflePass`) and by LDSM, MOVM, HMMA (`InstEmitAmpereMma.cs` `AFragments`: the registers' words stored once, then HMMA's A and B read four lanes' words at a time; words an earlier LDSM, MOVM or HMMA of the block read come from a cache, `EmitterContext.Fragments`, emptied where `InstEmitAmpere.cs` `Forget` sees the register written, and a run of LDSMs or of MOVMs exchanges all its words at once; MOVM also leaves its result's B words, read from the same exchange kept in column order (`WarpScratch` `Column`), for the HMMAs after (`EmitterContext.Written`, cached once the result lands); LDSM's results are also stored once in a mirror, `warp_mirror`, a slot a register, `WarpScratch.Mirror`, `ResourceManager.MirrorSlot`, while the shader's workgroup memory stays within 32 KB, from which HMMAs in later blocks read them while the register is unchanged: `InstEmitAmpere.cs` tracks `EmitterContext.Mirrored` from the held result's landing on, through the blocks all of whose predecessors left it) and MATCH (`AWarp`); the array's elements are `uvec4` (an IR `Load` with four destinations, `EmitterContext.LoadVector4`; `StructuredProgram` and `CodeGen/Spirv` `GetStoragePointer` take a vector at one index of a vector memory). Ballots there take their predicate's bits from it too, with only the active lanes' mask from a ballot (`InstEmitWarp.cs` `EmitBallot`): the Adreno 750 gave a shader's ballots of different predicates one value. Other stages keep subgroup shuffles and ballots. The Adreno 750 stages `OpGroupNonUniformShuffle` through local memory over the shader's own shared memory: Donkey Kong Bananza's upscaler read its weights back with other lanes' shuffled values in their low halves (2026-11-04). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- Ampere's half pairs as halves: the IR instruction `HalfPair` (add, multiply, fused multiply-add, minimum, maximum of the two halves packed in each 32-bit source; `CodeGen/Spirv` an `f16vec2`, chained ones without bitcasts) for HADD2, HMUL2, HFMA2 and HMNMX2 without .F32 (`InstEmitAmpereAlu.cs` `AHalfWord`); they had been unpacked to floats and packed back through `PackHalf2x16`'s integer rounding. Ampere code packs halves with `PackHalf2x16Rte` (the IR's `PackHalf2x16`, in SPIR-V two conversions to f16, rounded to nearest by the `RoundingModeRTE` that `shader_vk.py` adds after spirv-opt), and HMMA multiplies in fp32 for both accumulators (on the Adreno 750 fp32 FMAs run at twice fp16's rate and four times f16vec2's). Needs `shaderFloat16`, which Switch 2 hardware-class devices have (2026-11-04). Marked `nxnative:` in the code.

- `Instructions/InstEmitAmpere.cs` `AMapC0`: NVN2 compute's dispatch workgroup counts at c[0] + 4 are read from c[0] + 0x200, where the host writes them (Donkey Kong Bananza's tile depth bounds read 0). `InstEmitAmpereAlu.cs`: HFMA2's `.H0_NH1` (bit 86) rotates B (its low lane takes B's high half negated, its high lane B's low half), and MUFU.F16 applies its source's modifiers, as upstream nxnative's frontend does (2026-11-04).

The shader translation tool in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate` references them to translate the original Switch shaders to SPIR-V.
